Question:
Use `faker_qa/job_provider_empty_jobs_indexerror_uncaught/files/testcase.py`, class `TestJobProviderEmptyJobsIndexErrorUncaughtQA`, method `test_job_provider_empty_jobs_indexerror_uncaught_case`. After `seed_instance(2207)`, the test calls `job`, `job_male`, and `job_female` on the default locale (so `job_female` may delegate to `job` when no `jobs_female` list exists). It then resolves the `faker.providers.job` provider via `Generator.provider` and assigns `jobs` to an empty tuple, mutating shared provider state. The final `fake.job()` call enters `faker/providers/job/__init__.py::Provider.job` (lines 649–650), which calls `random_element(self.jobs)` on an empty sequence. What exact exception type and exception message are thrown as an uncaught exception from that `job` invocation (i.e., the exception that propagates out of the job provider and is caught by the test harness)?
